CausalChain: Chemotherapy (e.g., gemcitabine) → Increased CLDN18.2 expression and membrane exposure → Enhanced binding and cytotoxic action of CLDN18.2-targeted agents (mAbs, CAR-T, ADCs) → Induction of tumor cell death via ADCC/CDC → Release of tumor antigens and pro-inflammatory cytokines → Recruitment and activation of immune effector cells → Conversion of tumor microenvironment from immunologically cold to hot
Hypothesis: Preconditioning CLDN18.2-positive tumors with agents that upregulate its surface expression will synergize with CLDN18.2-targeted immunotherapies to reprogram the tumor microenvironment, enhancing immune cell infiltration and overcoming resistance to conventional immunotherapeutics in advanced gastric cancer.
Abstract: In recent years, Claudin18.2 (CLDN18.2) has emerged as a promising target for immunotherapy in gastric and gastro‐esophageal cancers. Beyond its role as a cell adhesion protein at tight junctions, chemotherapy agents such as gemcitabine have been shown to upregulate surface expression of CLDN18.2, thereby increasing the susceptibility of tumor cells to targeted immunotherapeutics. Building on these observations, we propose that preconditioning tumors with selected chemotherapeutic agents can not only enhance CLDN18.2 expression and subsequent binding by targeted agents (e.g., monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, CAR‐T cells, or antibody‐drug conjugates) but also induce inflammatory cell death, release tumor antigens, and modulate the tumor microenvironment. This cascade may convert immunologically “cold” tumors into more “hot” ones, ultimately increasing infiltration and activation of cytotoxic immune effector cells. In this review, we explore a novel hypothesis that controlled upregulation of CLDN18.2, when combined with precision immunotherapies, creates a feed‐forward mechanism for enhanced antitumor immune responses, providing a potential strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance in advanced gastric cancer.
